waypoints.name: Rameses / Goshen
waypoints.notes: Placed near the eastern Nile Delta and Qantir/Pi-Ramesses area as a common proxy; the biblical route's exact starting point is debated.

waypoints.name: Succoth in Egypt
waypoints.notes: Modeled in the Wadi Tumilat corridor; this is not the Succoth near the Jordan in Genesis.

waypoints.name: Etham
waypoints.notes: Regional proxy for Etham at the edge of the wilderness.

waypoints.name: Pi-hahiroth
waypoints.notes: Uses an OpenBible-listed Jabal Jinayfah plain candidate as a northern Gulf of Suez proxy; proposed Pi-hahiroth sites vary widely.

waypoints.name: Sea crossing proxy
waypoints.notes: Schematic midpoint for the Yam Suph / Red Sea crossing near the Pi-hahiroth proxy; not an archaeological claim.

waypoints.name: Wilderness of Shur / Etham
waypoints.notes: Regional proxy for the wilderness reached after the sea crossing, held west of Marah to keep the post-crossing route schematic.

waypoints.name: Marah
waypoints.notes: Placed at the Ain Hawarah candidate listed by OpenBible; the exact spring remains uncertain.

waypoints.name: Elim
waypoints.notes: Placed on an OpenBible Wadi Gharandel candidate for Elim.

waypoints.name: Red Sea camp
waypoints.notes: Numbers 33 lists a camp by the Red Sea after Elim; this is a schematic coastal waypoint.

waypoints.name: Wilderness of Sin
waypoints.notes: Regional proxy for the wilderness between Elim and Sinai.

waypoints.name: Rephidim
waypoints.notes: Placed near the Wadi Feiran tradition; the site remains debated.

waypoints.name: Mount Sinai / Horeb
waypoints.notes: Uses the traditional Jebel Musa proxy for Sinai/Horeb; other identifications exist.

waypoints.name: Kibroth-hattaavah
waypoints.notes: Placed near the Erweis el Ebeirig candidate listed by OpenBible; Numbers names the station but not exact coordinates.

waypoints.name: Hazeroth
waypoints.notes: Placed at the Ain el Khadra candidate listed by OpenBible; the exact location is uncertain.

waypoints.name: Wilderness of Paran
waypoints.notes: Regional desert proxy using OpenBible's high-confidence Paran isoband; this is not a precise campsite.

waypoints.name: Kadesh-barnea
waypoints.notes: Placed near the Ein el-Qudeirat / northeast Sinai tradition; the identification is debated.

waypoints.name: Wilderness of Zin
waypoints.notes: Regional proxy using OpenBible's high-confidence Zin isoband near Kadesh; this is not a precise campsite.

waypoints.name: Mount Seir / Edom
waypoints.notes: Regional proxy for the Edomite highlands and the Seir detour remembered in Deuteronomy.

waypoints.name: Mount Hor
waypoints.notes: Uses the Jebel Harun / Petra-region tradition for Mount Hor.

waypoints.name: Ezion-geber / Red Sea road
waypoints.notes: Aqaba/Eilat-area proxy for the Red Sea route around Edom.

waypoints.name: Zalmonah
waypoints.notes: Schematic stop from Numbers 33 after Mount Hor.

waypoints.name: Punon
waypoints.notes: Placed near the Faynan region as a common proxy for Punon.

waypoints.name: Oboth
waypoints.notes: Placed at the OpenBible Gharandal candidate for Oboth; the station remains approximate.

waypoints.name: Ije-abarim
waypoints.notes: Placed at the OpenBible Medeineh candidate, east of Moab as described by Numbers.

waypoints.name: Zered Valley
waypoints.notes: Uses an OpenBible Wadi al Hasa candidate for Zered, treated as an approximate crossing proxy.

waypoints.name: Arnon Valley
waypoints.notes: Uses the Wadi Mujib / Arnon corridor as the named Moab-Amorite border region.

waypoints.name: Beer and Mattanah
waypoints.notes: Combined schematic waypoint for the Beer and Mattanah itinerary in Numbers 21.

waypoints.name: Bamoth in Moab
waypoints.notes: Regional high-place proxy in Moab.

waypoints.name: Mount Nebo / Pisgah
waypoints.notes: Traditional Nebo/Pisgah proxy overlooking the Jordan valley and Jericho.

waypoints.name: Plains of Moab / Shittim
waypoints.notes: Placed at the OpenBible Tall Kafrayn candidate for Abel-shittim/Shittim near the plains of Moab.

waypoints.name: Jordan crossing by Jericho
waypoints.notes: Modeled opposite Jericho as Joshua 3-4 describes; the exact crossing point is not identified.

waypoints.name: Gilgal near Jericho
waypoints.notes: Placed at the OpenBible Khirbet el Mefjir candidate for Gilgal near Jericho.

paths.title: Rameses to Succoth
paths.notes: The first march out of Egypt is named in Exodus 12 and repeated in the Numbers 33 itinerary.

paths.title: Succoth to Etham

paths.title: Etham to Pi-hahiroth
paths.notes: The route turns back toward Pi-hahiroth before the sea, following the textual turn rather than a shortest path.

sourceRefs.label: TheTorah: Pi-hahiroth, Migdol, Baal-zephon, and Yam Suf

paths.title: Sea crossing to the wilderness
paths.notes: The sea crossing is schematic. The map shows the narrative passage through the sea and arrival in the wilderness, not a claim for a specific crossing site.

paths.title: Wilderness of Shur to Marah
paths.notes: Exodus describes three days in the wilderness before Marah; the endpoint is traditional and approximate.

sourceRefs.label: LDS Bible Map 2: Marah on the possible route

paths.title: Marah to Elim
paths.notes: The route reaches Elim, described as a water-rich camp.

sourceRefs.label: LDS Bible Map 2: Elim on the possible route

paths.title: Elim to the Red Sea camp
paths.notes: Numbers 33 adds a camp by the Red Sea between Elim and the Wilderness of Sin.

sourceRefs.label: Numbers 33:10: Elim to the Red Sea camp

paths.title: Red Sea camp to the Wilderness of Sin
paths.notes: Exodus places the Wilderness of Sin between Elim and Sinai; Numbers gives the camp sequence.

Bible Mapper Atlas: route timing to the Wilderness of Sin
LDS Bible Map 2: Wilderness of Sin

paths.title: Wilderness of Sin to Rephidim
paths.notes: The path follows the Numbers 33 sequence through Dophkah and Alush before Rephidim; those minor stops are modeled as curve points.

paths.title: Rephidim to Mount Sinai
paths.notes: The people leave Rephidim and camp in the wilderness of Sinai.

sourceRefs.label: OpenBible Atlas: Rephidim and Sinai candidates
Bible Mapper Atlas: Sinai route criteria and alternate Sinai placement

paths.title: Sinai to the Wilderness of Paran
paths.notes: Numbers carries the camp from Sinai through Kibroth-hattaavah and Hazeroth before the Wilderness of Paran.

sourceRefs.label: OpenBible Atlas: Kibroth-hattaavah, Hazeroth, and Paran candidates

paths.title: Paran to Kadesh-barnea
paths.notes: The spies return to Kadesh after searching the land; Deuteronomy remembers the march from Horeb to Kadesh-barnea.

sourceRefs.label: Bible Mapper Atlas: Horeb to Kadesh-barnea distance criterion

paths.title: The long wilderness turn
paths.notes: The forty-year period cannot be mapped as a precise route. This loop shows the commanded turn toward the wilderness and the long Seir/Edom orbit remembered by Deuteronomy.

sourceRefs.label: Numbers 14:25: turn into the wilderness by the Red Sea
Deuteronomy 2:1 and 2:14: Seir and the thirty-eight years

paths.title: Kadesh to Mount Hor
paths.notes: After Edom refuses passage, the congregation journeys from Kadesh to Mount Hor.

sourceRefs.label: Numbers 20:14-22: Kadesh, Edom, and Mount Hor
LDS Bible Map 2: Kadesh-barnea and Mount Hor

paths.title: Mount Hor by the Red Sea road
paths.notes: Numbers says Israel traveled from Mount Hor by the way of the Red Sea to compass Edom; this follows the Arabah toward the Gulf of Aqaba proxy.

sourceRefs.label: Numbers 21:4: Mount Hor by the way of the Red Sea
LDS Bible Map 2: Ezion-geber and Edom detour

paths.title: Red Sea road to Oboth
paths.notes: The Numbers 33 itinerary resumes northward through Zalmonah and Punon before Oboth.

paths.title: Oboth to Ije-abarim
paths.notes: The camp moves from Oboth to Ije-abarim, before Moab toward the sunrise.

paths.title: Ije-abarim to the Arnon
paths.notes: Numbers moves from Ije-abarim toward the brook Zered and then the Arnon border region.

sourceRefs.label: OpenBible Atlas: Zered and Arnon candidates

paths.title: Arnon to Pisgah
paths.notes: Numbers 21 lists Beer, Mattanah, Nahaliel, Bamoth, and a valley in Moab toward Pisgah; the middle stops are modeled schematically.

sourceRefs.label: Numbers 33:45-47: Dibon-gad to Abarim before Nebo
OpenBible Atlas: Bamoth, Nebo, and Pisgah candidates

paths.title: Pisgah to the Plains of Moab
paths.notes: The itinerary ends in the plains of Moab by Jordan near Jericho, from Beth-jesimoth to Abel-shittim.

sourceRefs.label: Numbers 33:48-49: Plains of Moab by Jordan near Jericho
Numbers 22:1: Plains of Moab by Jordan near Jericho
LDS Bible Map 2: Plains of Moab

paths.title: Moses ascends Nebo
paths.notes: This is a Moses-focused branch from the plains of Moab up to Nebo/Pisgah; it is part of the journey's narrative closure rather than the whole camp's movement.

sourceRefs.label: Deuteronomy 34:1: Moses goes from Moab to Nebo/Pisgah
OpenBible Atlas: Deuteronomy Nebo and Pisgah candidates

paths.title: Jordan crossing to Gilgal
paths.notes: Joshua moves the people from Shittim to the Jordan and then to Gilgal on the east border of Jericho. The crossing point is schematic.

sourceRefs.label: Joshua 3:1 and 3:14-17: Shittim to Jordan crossing
LDS Bible Map 2: Jordan crossing and Gilgal
OpenBible Atlas: Joshua Jordan, Gilgal, and Jericho candidates
